description: What this plugin believes Claude Code can do, and how each belief was established. One file so that a platform refresh is a diff against a checked model rather than a re-reading of every document.
why: This repository has been wrong in both directions. It emitted permissionDecision "escalate" for ten versions, a value the CLI does not accept, so every escalate-tier rule silently allowed the command it described. It also documented `effort` as unsupported on plugin agents when the CLI validates it.

Both mistakes were cheap to make because each belief lived in prose, in a different file, established at a different time, with no record of how it was checked. A capability the code depends on should say how it was verified and when.

evidence_levels.contract: Declared in the CLI's own schema. The strongest evidence short of running it.
evidence_levels.empirical: Observed on the wire in this environment.
evidence_levels.documented: Stated in the published documentation and not independently confirmed here.
evidence_levels.absent: Checked for and not found. An absence that can be relied on.

hook.SubagentStart.additionalContext.note: Declared as `hookEventName:Tt("SubagentStart"),additionalContext:O().optional()` and confirmed on the wire: a subagent reported back a token that existed nowhere but the hook's output.

hook.SubagentStop.last_assistant_message.note: Carries agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message and agent_transcript_path.

hook.TaskCompleted.can_block.note: Carries task_id, task_subject, task_description. No hookSpecificOutput, so it cannot inject or rewrite; exit 2 blocks the completion. Useful as a gate, not as an orchestrator.

hook.TaskCreated.carries_dependencies.note: No blocks, blockedBy, owner or metadata in the payload. This is why the task graph is the plugin's own artifact rather than a mirror of Claude Code's list.

hook.PermissionRequest.fires_headless.note: Did not fire under `claude -p` in any probed configuration, including auto and dontAsk modes. Nothing here depends on it.

permission_decision.values.note: allow, deny, ask, defer. A value outside this set is discarded and the tool call PROCEEDS.

agent_frontmatter.effort.note: Validated against low, medium, high, xhigh, max or an integer.

agent_frontmatter.ignored_for_plugins.note: permissionMode, hooks and mcpServers are warned about and discarded on a plugin agent. Setting one would be configuration that does nothing.

agent_teams.note: Requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS. Interactive only: under -p a named spawn degrades to a background subagent. Nothing in the lifecycle may depend on it.

worktree_isolation.note: isolation: worktree on a spawn or in agent frontmatter. worktree.baseRef defaults to fresh, so an isolated worker does not see unpushed local commits.

native_task_list.note: TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList backed by ~/.claude/tasks/<listId>/. Real blocks and blockedBy edges. Gated behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS on some models. Execution state on one machine, which is why it is not the system of record here.

dynamic_workflows.note: A workflows/ directory at the plugin root, JavaScript only, runs under -p. Unused: the lifecycle is declarative on purpose, and this suits repository-wide fan-out rather than stage progression.

lsp_servers.note: A .lsp.json at the plugin root. Deliberately not shipped: extensionToLanguage is not variable-expanded and extension claims are global across plugins, so a placeholder would outrank a project's real server.

refresh: When the tested_against version moves, re-verify every capability marked load_bearing before anything else. Those are the ones whose failure is silent.
